headline: Chinese tech stocks have become the biggest losers of the global AI sell-off, with the Star50 index down nearly 40% this half-year.
score_reason: Bloomberg reporting, read in full, shows China's tech market hit hardest, with a funding risk for its AI firms; one outlet only.
importance_line: Investors who bought into the spring rally in Chinese tech shares lose most, then Chinese AI firms that rely on selling shares to raise money, and the open question is whether state-backed buying, which regulators urged on Thursday, can stop the slide.
summary: Bloomberg reports that the Star50 index, China's Nasdaq-style board of technology companies, has fallen nearly 40% in the current half year, the worst of any major tech gauge worldwide, with chipmakers MetaX and Moore Threads each losing about half their value. Leonid Mironov, portfolio manager at Gavekal Capital, says shares are "the default source" of funding for China's AI firms, and Bloomberg calls the slump a setback for Beijing's plan to use stock markets to drive its tech ambitions.
